c_padcool: Wet-pad cooling at the hottest hour
c_strip2: Evaporative cooling works best in dry air.

c_sub: The same farm size, budget and priority at two places.

chat_bad_provider: LLM_PROVIDER in .env must be 'anthropic' or 'openai_compatible'. The dashboard works without the assistant.
chat_card_sub: The assistant reads the plan first, then answers your questions. Every number is checked.
chat_error: The assistant is unavailable right now. The plan and dashboard above are still correct.
chat_footer: The AI explains and compares; you make the final decision.
chat_hello: Ask me anything about this plan.
chat_hello_sub: I explain the numbers and can re-run them. Write in English or Arabic.
chat_no_base_url: Set LLM_BASE_URL in your .env file to your open-source model server. The dashboard works without it.
chat_no_key: The assistant needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your .env file, or an open-source model (see README). The dashboard works without it.
chat_no_llm_key: The assistant needs LLM_API_KEY (your OpenRouter key) in .env or in the app's Secrets. The dashboard works without it.
chat_placeholder: Ask about this plan, e.g. what if my budget is half?
chat_thinking: Checking the plan and running the tools…
cmp_add_sub: Optional: the same farm, budget and priority at a second place, side by side.
cmp_sub: Seven setups for {crop} at this site, on {area} m²
diagnostics_note: Light coverage uses growing days. VPD counts daylight hours above the crop limit. Electricity balances each hour with no battery; exported electricity earns zero by default. Thresholds and equipment performance remain estimates.
dust_hours: {n} hours above the scenario threshold out of {total} available hours.
dust_line: Last 30 days: {mean} µg/m³ dust on average, {n} of {total} hours above the dust-event level (CAMS / Open-Meteo).
dust_note: Recent CAMS model estimates from Open-Meteo, separate from the typical climate year. These are not a long-term dust forecast or measured site observations.
dust_scenario_note: Illustrative soiling rates affect light, solar output, yield, cleaning cost and water. They are editable CSV assumptions, not measured dust deposition.
dust_unavailable: Dust data unavailable. No exposure estimate has been substituted.
estimate_banner: Prices are FAOSTAT farm-gate prices and water use is calculated from this site's weather. Build costs and crop limits are still estimates, so treat profit and payback as illustrative. See Assumptions.
fc_hot: Days above the crop limit this week
fc_src: Next 7 days from the Open-Meteo forecast (free, no key).
fc_uv_n: 8 and above is very high: shade and cover workers
gis_heat_n: Hot panels make less power; plan cleaning and airflow
gis_src: EU Joint Research Centre PVGIS (SARAH3 satellite radiation, ERA5 weather, horizon from a digital elevation model).
gis_sub: Terrain-aware solar yield from the EU PVGIS map, and this week's heat, humidity and UV.
gis_tilt_n: Panels face {az}° on the compass (180° = south) · site elevation {elev} m
gis_title: Sun, heat and humidity: satellites, maps and forecast
gis_yield_n: PVGIS satellite radiation {years}, terrain shading included
h_data: Built on open data: NASA POWER · EU PVGIS · Open-Meteo · CAMS · FAOSTAT · FAO-56 · World Bank · OpenStreetMap
h_f1t: Satellite sun, heat, humidity and wind (NASA POWER), terrain-aware solar (PVGIS), dust (CAMS) and this week's forecast for the exact pin.
h_f2t: Eight crops against open field, shade net, wet-pad and chiller greenhouses, NIR screens and agrivoltaics, hour by hour, within your budget.
h_f3t: CapEx, OpEx, revenue at local FAOSTAT prices, water, NPV, IRR, break-even price and a downside case for every option.
h_feat_title: From a pin on the map to a bankable plan
h_k1t: Pick the site; Croptions picks the crop, the setup and the solar.
h_k2t: Add one kit pod per {area} m² when you build the setup.
h_k3t: The kit watches every leaf, warns early and advises the screen.
i_notes: Break-even is the crop price that makes the NPV zero; the last column shows payback if prices fall {down}%.
i_rate_fallback: The World Bank lending rate or inflation is not available for this country right now, so NPV uses the {rate}% fallback from data/settings.csv.
i_rate_wb: NPV uses a {rate}% real discount rate: World Bank lending rate {lending}% ({ly}) minus inflation {inflation}% ({iy}).
i_sub: Every setup for {crop}: what it costs, what it earns and how it holds up over {years} years.
k_cost_n: Everything needed to build this setup
k_solar_n: Sized for the hottest day's cooling
k_water_n: Crop irrigation plus cooling-pad water, calculated from local weather
kc_live_demo: Latest demo reading (simulated): leaf {leaf} °C · air {air} °C · humidity {rh}%
kc_note: Kit prices are estimates in data/settings.csv, not supplier quotes. No yield gain from the kit is assumed.
kc_pods_n: {price} QAR per pod, one per {area} m²
kc_sub: Sensor pods that watch the crop, warn early and advise the screen.
kd_hot_n: Minutes above the {limit} °C crop limit that day
kd_light_n: Smart screen compared with fixed shade
kd_note: This site's NASA typical-year weather in 10-minute steps: fixed agrivoltaic shade compared with a movable screen run by the same rule as the kit's advice. This is the kit benefit the app calculates; it is a simulation, not a measurement.
kd_pv: Solar energy with the smart screen
kd_smart_hot: Too hot with the smart screen
kd_title: Fixed shade vs the kit's smart screen: one simulated day
kit_code_unknown: Kit ID not found. Open the Croptions Kit page in the app to see your Kit ID.
kit_cwsi_n: 0 = cooling itself well, 1 = stopped; alert at {alert}
kit_cwsi_night: Needs daylight: leaves do not transpire at night
kit_dew_n: Below {alert} °C, water can condense on leaves (mould risk)
kit_dli_n: From readings received; the crop needs {need} a day
kit_ev_condensation: Leaves near dew point: ventilate (mould risk)
kit_ev_dry_air: Air too dry for the crop
kit_ev_leaf_hot: Leaf above the crop's heat limit
kit_last: Reading #{n} received at {at} UTC · crop time {hour}
kit_last_sent: Last sent: #{n} at {hour}: leaf {leaf} °C, air {air} °C, humidity {rh}%
kit_mode_approve_n: The kit suggests a screen position; nothing moves until you approve.
kit_mode_auto_n: The kit moves the screen by itself and logs why.
kit_mode_manual_n: You set the screen; the kit only shows its advice.
kit_remote_help: Open the Croptions Kit page in the app, then type its 4-digit Kit ID here.
kit_sim_banner: Demo tool: each button sends one simulated reading, built from this site's NASA weather, to the Kit ID above. Keep the Croptions Kit page open in another tab to watch it arrive.
kit_sub: The kit watches your crop's leaves, air and light, warns you early and advises the shade screen.
kit_thermal_sub: Illustrative image: the average leaf temperature matches the reading; the pattern is generated.
kit_waiting_sub: Readings appear here within two seconds of the kit sending them.
kit_watching_sub: Choose how much the kit may do on its own.
kp_f1t: Spots leaves heating up before they wilt.
kp_f2t: Tracks dry air (VPD) and dew point for mould risk.
kp_f3t: Auto, approve-first or manual control of the screen.
kp_f4t: Runs off its own panel; alerts in Arabic and English.
kp_price: From {price} QAR per pod + {service} QAR a year
kp_price_note: One pod per {area} m². Placeholder prices, not a supplier quote.
kp_sub: A solar-powered pod that watches the crop's leaves, air and light, warns you early and tells you when to move the shade screen, water or ventilate.
kp_title: Feel the heat before your crop does
l_eyebrow: Farm planning for hot, arid regions
l_hero: Turn desert sun into farms that grow and pay off.
l_sub: Drop a pin on the map. Croptions tells you what to grow and when, which setup survives the heat, how much solar power it needs, and how many years until it pays for itself.
none_budget: The setups that keep crops cool enough cost more than the budget.
none_constraints: No option passes all temperature, light, data and budget checks. Review the detailed reasons below.
none_nodata: No climate data for this site yet.
none_title: No setup works here with these inputs.
none_too_hot: No setup keeps any crop below its heat limit for 90% of the year.
operate_missing: Sunlight data is unavailable. Reanalyse this site with the updated NASA data before running the simulator.
p_empty: Click the map to drop a pin.
p_need_pin: Drop a pin on the map first
p_sub: Pick a site on the map, then tell us about the farm.
plan_updated: Plan updated: the dashboard now shows the new result
pr_payback_n: Earn back the build cost soonest
prices_country: FAOSTAT farm-gate prices for {country}, fetched {date}. Farm-gate is what a wholesaler pays the farmer; shop prices are higher.
prices_world: No site analysed yet, so these are world median FAOSTAT farm-gate prices (fetched {date}). Analyse a site to see its country's prices.
prices_world_site: The country for this site could not be looked up, so these are world median FAOSTAT farm-gate prices (fetched {date}).
profit_sub: Starts at minus the build cost; crosses zero at payback
r_empty_sub: Pick a site on the Plan page, then press Analyse this site.
reason_hold: Hold position to avoid unnecessary movement
reason_protect_light: Open the screen to preserve growing light
reason_reduce_heat: Close the screen gradually to reduce heat
reason_release_shade: Open the screen as the temperature falls
s1: Fetching climate data (NASA POWER, 5 years, hourly)
safe_answer_no_plan: Choose a site on the map and press Analyse first, then ask me about the plan.
safe_answer_none: No setup works for these inputs. {reason}
safe_answer_rec: The recommendation is {setup} for {crop}: it keeps the crop below its heat limit {coverage}% of the year, costs {capex} QAR to build and pays back in {payback} years.
sc_dli_n: {crop} needs at least {need}; the surplus is what shading can spend
sc_et0_n: FAO-56 reference evaporation outdoors; highest in {month} at {mm} mm/day
sc_haze_n: Sunlight lost to dust and haze compared with a clear sky
sc_hours_n: Hours a year above the {crop} limit of {limit} °C in the open field
sc_humid_n: Wet-bulb peaks at {wb} °C: the lowest air temperature wet pads can reach
sc_ir_n: Infrared part of sunlight: heat without growing light, which a heat-reflecting screen blocks
sc_peak_n: Average daily high in {month}; hottest hour of the typical year {max} °C
sc_source: Source: NASA POWER hourly, {years}, fetched {date}. Grid cells are about 50 km wide, so this is the region's climate, not a farm measurement.
sc_sub: The typical year behind every number above: hourly NASA POWER weather, averaged over five recent years.
sc_sun_n: {year} kWh/m² a year, which sizes the solar panels
sc_title: What NASA measured at this site
scan_note: Draw a rectangle on the map. Each point fetches climate data and may take a minute; nearby points can share the same coarse satellite grid. Maximum 25 points.
set_edit_hint: To change a value, edit the matching file in data/ and reload. Editing inside the app is planned.
set_note: Every value the planner uses, with its source. Prices come live from FAOSTAT; values marked estimate still need a real source.
share_hint: Anyone with this link sees the same plan.
solar_cap: That day the panels produce {solar} kWh and the chiller uses {cooling} kWh. Cooling at night needs storage or the grid, which the plan does not cost yet.
solar_none: No solar chiller option for this crop.
solar_sub: Solar chiller greenhouse in {month}: {kw} kW of panels vs cooling electricity, per hour
sources_sub: Every number traces back to these
suggest_budget: What if my budget is half?
suggest_crop: Which crop fits this site best?
suggest_water: Which option uses the least water?
temp_cap_none: No setup stays below {limit} °C every month.

temp_cap_pad: The wet-pad greenhouse goes above the limit in {months}.
temp_title: Inside temperature vs the heat limit
